content.text: No licence runs from SFJ to us in this agreement — the structure gives us ownership instead. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: In consideration of the Approval Payments to be made under this Agreement (if and to the extent applicable), and in further consideration of the payment by PB to SFJ of [***], SFJ shall sell and transfer to PB, and PB shall acquire from SFJ, the sole and exclusive ownership, even as to SFJ, of the Trial Data Package including all Research Results as set forth below in this Section 11.1.1.4.
input.rationale: This is a clinical development funding agreement, not a supply/licence deal, and there is no counterparty-to-customer licence grant anywhere in it (searches for grant language return only PB's security-interest grant to SFJ at p0537). The rule's protective purpose is satisfied on better-than-preferred terms: PB retains sole and exclusive ownership of all Existing PB Intellectual Property and of all Trial Inventions regardless of inventorship (p0650, p0651, p0659), SFJ and its Affiliates and Permitted Third Parties assign Trial Inventions to PB, and SFJ's interim ownership of the Trial Data Package is converted into PB's "sole and exclusive ownership, even as to SFJ" (p0663), with Research Results treated at all times as PB's Confidential Information (PB as disclosing Party) pre-transfer. Ownership is perpetual and irrevocable by definition, needs no affiliate/contractor extension, and passes with a permitted assignment to a successor (Section 15.6, referenced in the Licensing Transaction definition at p0146). The only grants running the other way (security interest, sublicensing constraints in p0084/p0146, Permitted Lien carve-out at p0598) restrict us rather than licence us and are the subject of other rules, so no redline here. Note for the file: the agreement contains no express interim licence for PB to use the Trial Data Package before the purchase closes; PB's disclosing-Party status over Research Results and its regulatory access rights make this a drafting nicety rather than a material gap.
